Alex —

Thanks for the RFP, looks clear. High level response below and I attached a short proposal that frames a single commercial construct we use with customers facing similar risk profiles: an Anchor + Backstop framework (pdf attached). Key points:

- Anchor: 6–12 month committed bucket sized to baseline steady-state (discounted rate, predictable unit economics).
- Backstop: short-term onboarding credits tied to measured SLO misses during rollout (3–6 week window). This protects you during early tuning without requiring a large upfront buyout.
- Burst support: dedicated burst pool + autoscale policy for daytime spikes (metered at a higher per-token rate but capped).
- Technical carveouts: we can exclude very high egress jobs from committed consumption and bill them at consumption rates to avoid overcommitting your egress budget.

Short ask: can we schedule a 45-minute working call tomorrow to align on the baseline anchor size and your KPI thresholds for the backstop? I’ll bring a concise term sheet and Karthik will run through the runtime handoff.

Attached: anchor_backstop_proposal_v1.pdf (pricing model + term sheet sketch).

Hi Alex —

Quick technical notes to ground the pricing tradeoffs Vanessa outlined:

- KV cache sensitivity: if your agent relies on long prefix reuse, committed capacity enables persistent KV warm pools which meaningfully reduce per-token latency for interactive sessions. That converts directly into lower billable tokens because of fewer retries and shorter prompt engineering loops.
- Egress carveouts: we recommend tagging high-egress pipelines (batch exports + analytics) so they’re excluded from committed buckets — billed at a consumption uplift but not counted toward Anchor utilization.
- Quantization/packing: for typical LLM families we can deploy 4-bit quantized variants for the bulk of offline embedding/embedding-ops to reduce cost; interactive routes can remain on higher-fidelity variants pinned to the anchor.
- Runtime parity proof: we can provide a 48-hour parity test run on a representative workload (we mirror your traffic trace) and produce latency percentiles and token-cost reconciliation before you sign.

I’ll prepare a short ops note for the call outlining handoff checkpoints (KV warm pool sizing, prefix routing, and rollback policy).

—Karthik
